name: Prompt Diff & History
blurb: two versions of a prompt compared word by word with the token change, and versions kept per project
intro: Compares two versions of a prompt sentence by sentence and word by word (moved sentences found as moves), gives the token change per section and says which instructions, rules (modal verbs, limits), examples and output-format lines changed; keeps the versions with a note on why each changed.

examples.title: Two texts directly: a diff-summary prompt made into a release-note prompt

input.left:
Summarize the diff below in one sentence. Do not mention file names.

<diff>
{{diff}}
</diff>
input.right:
Summarize the diff below in at most two sentences for a release note. Mention a file name only when the change is limited to it.

<diff>
{{diff}}
</diff>

Start with the user-visible effect.

usage: Give left and right (two prompt texts) to compare them directly, or history (a JSON list of {label, at, note, text}, oldest first) with from and to (1-based indices; empty = the last two). Returns token counts before/after (estimates), words added/removed, sentences changed/added/removed/moved, a 'what changed' table (instruction added/removed/reworded, rule changed with the modal verbs or numbers before and after, example changed, moved), tokens per section, the version list, a unified diff (GNU diff -u format) and a Markdown changelog of the whole history. Use it when reviewing a prompt change, writing its commit message or explaining a behaviour change after a prompt edit.
sources: GNU diffutils manual, 'Unified Format' (diff -u hunks and headers)
Hunt & McIlroy, 'An Algorithm for Differential File Comparison' (1976), and Myers, 'An O(ND) Difference Algorithm and Its Variations' (1986): longest-common-subsequence alignment
RFC 2119 (MUST, SHOULD, MAY) for the strength of modal verbs in rules
Token estimate: chars/4 rule of thumb and a word-piece heuristic; not an exact tokenizer
